description: BTIDES ATT packet information data types

0xD2_ATT_SIGNED_WRITE_CMD.description: Structure for ATT\_SIGNED\_WRITE\_CMD packet. Write without response with an authentication signature appended. Per spec, shall not be used on an Enhanced ATT bearer.

opcode_str.description: This optional field is just for if you don't care about json file size and you want more human-readable JSON output.

attribute_handle.description: The handle of the attribute to be set.

value_hex_str.description: The value to be written to the attribute, as a hex string. May be 0 octets in length.

utf8_str.description: This is an optional human-readable version of the value being written.

authentication_signature_hex_str.$comment: Per Vol 3, Part F, Section 3.3.1, the authentication signature is the SignCounter (4 octets) concatenated with the MAC (8 octets), for a total of 12 octets / 24 hex characters.
authentication_signature_hex_str.description: 12-byte authentication signature (SignCounter || MAC) covering the opcode, attribute handle, and attribute value, as a 24-character hex string.

0xD2_ATT_SIGNED_WRITE_CMD2.description: Structure for ATT\_SIGNED\_WRITE\_CMD packet, as single raw hex string.

opcode_str.description: This optional field is just for if you don't care about json file size and you want more human-readable JSON output.

0x52_ATT_WRITE_CMD.description: Structure for ATT\_WRITE\_CMD packet. Write without response; the server generates no ATT_ERROR_RSP or ATT_WRITE_RSP for this command.

opcode_str.description: This optional field is just for if you don't care about json file size and you want more human-readable JSON output.

attribute_handle.description: The handle of the attribute to be set.

value_hex_str.description: The value to be written to the attribute, as a hex string. May be 0 octets in length.

utf8_str.description: This is an optional human-readable version of the value being written.

0x52_ATT_WRITE_CMD2.description: Structure for ATT\_WRITE\_CMD packet, as single raw hex string.

opcode_str.description: This optional field is just for if you don't care about json file size and you want more human-readable JSON output.

0x23_ATT_MULTIPLE_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF.description: Structure for ATT\_MULTIPLE\_HANDLE\_VALUE\_NTF packet. Server-initiated notification of two or more attribute values at once.

opcode_str.description: This optional field is just for if you don't care about json file size and you want more human-readable JSON output.

handle_length_value_tuple_list.description: List of Handle Length Value Tuples, one per attribute being notified. Per spec the server shall not truncate a tuple.

attribute_handle.description: The handle of the attribute being notified.

value_length.description: Length in octets of the Attribute Value field for this tuple.

value_hex_str.description: The current value of the attribute, as a hex string.

utf8_str.description: This is an optional human-readable version of the value.

0x23_ATT_MULTIPLE_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF2.description: Structure for ATT\_MULTIPLE\_HANDLE\_VALUE\_NTF packet, as single raw hex string.

opcode_str.description: This optional field is just for if you don't care about json file size and you want more human-readable JSON output.
This optional field is just for if you don't care about json file size and you want more human-readable JSON output.

length_value_tuple_list.description: List of Length Value Tuples, in the order corresponding to the handles in the request.

value_length.description: Length in octets of the Attribute Value field for this tuple (the announced length, not necessarily the actual length received if the tuple list was truncated to fit the PDU).

value_hex_str.description: The attribute value, as a hex string. If the tuple was truncated, the length of this string in octets may be less than value_length.

utf8_str.description: This is an optional human-readable version of the value.

set_of_values_hex_str.$comment: The ATT protocol does not delimit boundaries between concatenated values here; the client must know each attribute's fixed size (except the last, which may be variable). So we store the concatenated raw bytes as a single hex string.
